armory.look.ashbound.source: A chain of glowing iron winds round the arms, from the shoulders to the wrists. Ash falls from it.

armory.look.breachbrand.source: Fire runs along the weapon from the grip to the point, and drips from the tip.

armory.look.burningcrown.source: A circlet of molten iron, with horns of flame and a door of white fire at the brow. Embers lift off the points.

armory.look.cinderstride.source: Low flames lick up the shins from a ring of coal at each ankle. Each step leaves an ember on the ground that burns out.

armory.look.crystalspurs.source: Small spurs of crystal along both arms, each a different size. Their colors shift slowly from amethyst to aqua to rose.

armory.look.emberheart.source: A cracked coal burns in the chest and beats like a heart. Fire runs out along its veins with every beat.

armory.look.eternalarmlets.source: Engraved bands of blue-violet fire circle the upper arms and the wrists. Flames lick up off them.

armory.look.eternaledge.source: A blade of blue-violet light runs along the weapon's edge. Sparks trail from it when you swing.

armory.look.eternalgreaves.source: Blue-violet fire wraps the legs from the knee to the foot, under a lattice of light. Sparks rise as you walk.

armory.look.eternalhalo.source: A band of blue-violet fire turns over the head, runes round it and the Origin's spark at its front.

armory.look.eternalset.source: All five Eternal pieces at once: the Halo, the Sigil, the Armlets, the Greaves and the Edge.

armory.look.eternalsigil.source: The Origin's dragon of light circles the spark on the chest, biting its own tail. A slow light runs round it.

armory.look.insigniaarmlet.source: A gilt band round the left upper arm, enamelled in your guild's colors, with its arms on a shield of beaten gold.

cards.iliacSet.banishDaedra.rules.source: Destroy the weakest enemy daedra unit here.

cards.iliacSet.clavicusVile.flavor.source: A bargain. Read the small print later.

cards.iliacSet.egCairnkeeper.flavor.source: Every soul pays the tithe. The Keeper counts them all.

features.armoryOthers.note.source: Whose Aura Armory pieces are shown. Near shows the players close to you. Your own pieces always show.

features.dungeonEncounters.note.source: Some dungeon rooms hold an encounter: a ward to hold against foes, sources or seals to break, or a puzzle to work out. Win one to open its vault. Online, your party wins it together.

features.killFxOthers.note.source: Whose kill effects and mount looks are shown. Near shows the players close to you. Your own always show.

features.livingAdventurers.note.source: Simulates rival adventurers delving dungeons across Tamriel, advancing, and leaving fallen remains.

features.livingBounties.note.source: Rebalances notice boards toward wilderness contracts with higher payouts that lower regional crisis tension.

features.livingCamps.note.source: Spawns slope-aligned roadside encampments, patrol outposts, and traveller tents along highways.

features.livingNaval.note.source: Populates open waters with multi-ship fleet skirmishes between provincial patrols and pirate squadrons.

features.livingNemesis.note.source: Dispatches persistent challengers, bounty hunters, and grudge avengers with roleplay dialogue checks.

features.livingPolitical.note.source: Drives regional state transitions between peace, war, plague, and civil strife across Tamriel.

features.livingQuarantine.note.source: Bars city gates around the clock during severe outbreaks and establishes outside relief tents.

features.livingRoadAdventurers.note.source: Spawns non-hostile adventurers travelling highways, camping in the wilds, returning with dungeon spoils, or fighting monsters along the road.

features.livingTravel.note.source: Allows journeys and fast travel to be interrupted by roadside caravans, dilemmas, or hostile ambushes.

features.livingUrban.note.source: Generates contained street clashes between the city watch and insurgents during regional war and strife.

features.mod.kingsGambit.note.source: A game of armies and kings at a tavern's card table, against a regular or another player, for gold or for fun. Off, the tables offer only Hold'em and Iliac Hand.

features.mwItemIcons.note.source: With Morrowind data, items in your inventory and quickslots are shown as rendered 3D ground meshes. Off shows classic 2D item sprites.

features.mwModelDetail.note.source: With the Morrowind body, Pixelated draws bodies, horses and your arms in large pixels like the classic sprites. Sharp draws them at your screen’s full resolution and uses more video memory.

features.mwPlayerBody.note.source: With Morrowind data, your character is drawn in 3D: hands and weapons in first person, full body in third person, and a 3D figure in the inventory. Off keeps classic 2D sprites and the paperdoll.

features.offlineFirmament.note.source: Enables the Firmament constellation passive tree and Renown progression while playing offline.

features.offlineHousing.note.source: Buy and sell homes at the front door across all towns and hamlets, as in online DFO. Off restores classic bank housing.

features.offlineProfessions.note.source: Enables gathering nodes (mining, herbs, logging, hunting, fishing) and crafting professions offline.

features.questlines.effect.source: Takes effect on the next quest you take; quests you already have keep the rules they began with.

features.questlines.note.source: Every quest shows its objectives, some let you choose how they end, some offer a piece of gear fitted to you when done, and questlines lead to the Breaches, the Battlespire and the Abyss. Off is the classic journal and its rewards, and online it is always on.

features.resourceHighlights.note.source: How herbs, veins, trees and other gathering spots near you stand out. Glint makes them catch the light with sparkles; Outline rings each one in its profession’s color, plain to see day or night; Both does both.

features.wildlife.note.source: Birds, bats and small animals live outdoors. Flocks cross the sky, birds sit on roofs and fly off as you come near, and small animals run from your feet.

Your review is {days, plural, =0 {at your next visit to the guild's hall} one {at the guild's hall in # day or later} other {at the guild's hall in # days or later}}: below {expel} you are expelled, and it ends only once one skill reaches {high}, a second {low}, and your standing is 0 or more.

guild.rankNeeds.falls.source: Your review {days, plural, =0 {at your next visit to the guild's hall} one {at the guild's hall in # day or later} other {at the guild's hall in # days or later}} lowers you to {title}.

guild.rankNeeds.fallsRep.source: Your review {days, plural, =0 {at your next visit to the guild's hall} one {at the guild's hall in # day or later} other {at the guild's hall in # days or later}} lowers you to {title}: {current} needs reputation {need}.

guild.rankNeeds.highBest.source: A guild skill at {bar} - your best, {skill}, is {value}

guild.rankNeeds.paced.source: {days, plural, =1 {Earliest promotion: tomorrow} other {Earliest promotion: in # days}}

guild.rankNeeds.reputationOwed.source: Reputation {have} of {need} ({owed} more already earned, arriving at most {max} a real day)

guild.rankNeeds.seat.source: Ranks {officer} and {master} are each chapter's council and Master, won only by Merit

guild.rankNeeds.seatMerit.source: At each Sunday's Turning the chairs go to the members with the most Merit over the last {weeks} weeks, with {days} real days in the guild and accounts {age} real days old

guild.ranks.about.source: A guild has {min} to {max} ranks. New members join at the lowest.

guild.ranks.moving.source: If you save, {count, plural, one {# member moves} other {# members move}} to {rank}.

guild.ranks.powersAbout.source: The guildmaster may do all of it. A rank acts only on the ranks under its own.

guild.ranks.reset.done.source: The permissions are back to the defaults.

guild.requests.about.source: Type a guild's tag. Its officers see your request and answer it.

guild.requests.days.source: sent {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago

guild.requests.why.tag.source: a tag of 2 to 4 letters or digits

guild.seatService.source: Rank {rank} offers this. Online, ranks {officer} and {master} are chapter chairs won by Merit, and a chair's services are at its own chapter's halls, for a member at rank {cap}. A notice board explains chapters.

guild.shop.intro.source: Everything here costs silver. Your own wares come from your silver. Hall furniture comes from the silver treasury.

guild.shop.look.banker.source: A banker's counter for the hall. Members press it to open the guild vault.

guild.shop.look.brazier.source: An iron brazier that burns and lights the hall.

guild.shop.look.crestplaque.source: The guild's arms on a wooden shield for the hall's wall.

guild.shop.look.guildcrest.source: Your guild's arms in your portrait, where other players see your face.

guild.shop.look.guildsails.source: Patterned sails for every ship on your account, with your guild's arms on them.

guild.shop.look.insigniaarmlet.source: Your guild's arms on a gilded band round one upper arm. An Aura Armory piece for the arms slot.

guild.shop.look.standard.source: A tall pole with the guild's banner, for the hall.

guild.shop.look.throne.source: A high-backed seat with the guild's arms on its back. One to a guild.

guild.shop.look.wartable.source: A long table with a map of Tamriel and markers on it.

guild.shop.look.weaponrack.source: A rack of swords and spears under the guild's arms.

guild.shop.state.account.source: Bought once, for every character on your account.

guild.shop.state.guild.source: The guild owns {owned} of {max}. {placed} set down.

guild.shop.stock.none.source: Every {name} the guild owns is set down. Buy another on the guild's Shop page.

guild.shop.unread.source: The shop cannot be read now: {why}

guild.shop.use.furniture.source: Set it down in the guild hall with the decor tool.

guild.shop.use.guildcrest.source: Choose it as your portrait icon in your profile.

guild.shop.use.guildsails.source: Choose a pattern on a ship's Paint panel in the Fleet.

guild.shop.use.insigniaarmlet.source: Wear it from the Aura Armory, in the arms slot.

guild.shop.why.max.source: the guild owns the most it may

guild.wayBack.drift.source: Below 0 your standing also recovers a point {days, plural, one {every day} other {every # days}} of your own time. Rests and journeys count{online, select, yes {, and so does time logged off} other {}}.

guild.wayBack.paced.source: Online, quests and the recovery raise it by at most {max} a real day (days start at midnight UTC){owed, plural, =0 {} other {, with # more standing on the way}}. On top of that, a chapter writ of the guild's on a notice board adds {writ}.

guild.wayBack.quests.source: As a stranger you may still ask its quest-giver for work: each quest done raises your standing {per}{n, plural, =0 {} one { - # more quest reaches {need}} other { - # more quests reach {need}}}.

guild.wayBack.shut.source: This hall is shut this Season. The guild's halls in other regions still give work.

guild.wayBack.skills.source: It also asks one of its guild skills at {high} and a second at {low}: {skills}.

guild.wayBack.standing.source: Your standing here is {rep}. It takes members at {need} or more.

home.goneBack.source: {n, plural, one {One of your things stood in a home your account no longer holds, and came back to your pack.} other {# of your things stood in a home your account no longer holds, and came back to your pack.}}

home.hall.saleAsk.source: Sell the hall of {name} for {gold} gold, and half of what its placed pieces cost?

home.hall.saleTreasury.source: The gold goes to the guild's treasury. The pieces go with the hall.

home.hall.saleVault.source: The guild's vault stays the guild's.

home.hall.sold.source: You sold the hall of {name}. {gold} gold went to the guild's treasury.

housing.transfer.badName.source: That is not an account name.

housing.transfer.confirm.source: Offer this house to {to} for {price} gold. {kept}.

housing.transfer.leaveFurnishings.source: Leave the furnishings with the house?

housing.transfer.leaveGoods.source: Leave the goods in its chests and stalls?

housing.transfer.offerOut.source: An offer for this house is already out.

housing.transfer.price.source: Price in gold (0 is a gift):

housing.transfer.sent.source: The offer is out. It stands for three days.

housing.transfer.unsent.source: The offer could not be sent.

hunt.mark.doneWeek.source: You have slain this week's named beast.

hunt.mark.dropped.source: You gave up the hunt for {title}.

hunt.mark.gaveUp.source: You gave up the hunt for {title}.

hunt.mark.gone.source: That notice has been taken down.

hunt.mark.heldAlready.source: You are already hunting a named beast.

hunt.mark.lapsed.source: The week is over. {title} has gone to ground.

hunt.mark.meta.source: Named beast · Tier {tier} · {gold} gold · a trophy

hunt.mark.paidLine.source: Named beast slain: {title}. +{gold} gold and its trophy.

hunt.mark.paidStory.source: Word of {title}'s death reaches {town} before you do. The hunters send a heavy purse, and the beast is yours to mount.

hunt.mark.rewardHint.source: a mounted trophy of the beast, to hang in your home

hunt.mark.rewardLine.source: Reward: {gold} gold pieces and its mounted trophy.

hunt.mark.rung.source: Named beasts are posted to Stalkers and above.

hunt.mark.slainWeek.source: You have slain this week's named beast. A new one is posted at the Turning.

hunt.mark.spotted.source: You find the tracks of {title}, {m} meters away. It knows you are here.

hunt.mark.story.source: {title} has been seen {far} {dir} of {town}. It has killed hunters before. Bring it down this week.

hunt.mark.taken.source: You took the hunt for {title}. It is marked on your map.

hunt.mark.tookLine.source: Taken: {title}. Look for the black circle on your map.

hunt.mark.where.source: Where: {far} {dir} of {town}. Marked on your map with a black circle.

hunt.standing.account.source: Your account: {n} bounties. The title {title} at {at}.

hunt.standing.accountAll.source: Your account: {n} bounties. Every hunt title is yours.

hunt.standing.marks.source: Named beasts slain: {n}. The boards post one a week.

hunt.standing.marksAt.source: At {rung}, the boards post you a named beast each week.

hunt.trophy.hunted.source: A trophy of the {beast}. It is in your pack.

input.action.professions.source: Open your Professions page, or the Crafting page at a station

instance.door.castleLine.source: Enter the shared castle, or your guild's own? Only your guild's members can enter it.

instance.door.holdLine.source: Privateer's Hold is closed to the public. You may enter an instance of your own, for you and your party.

instance.door.line.source: Enter the shared world, or an instance of your own for you and your party?

instance.door.questHere.source: Your quest's business here waits in your instance.

instance.door.questPublic.source: Your quest's business here is only in your instance. The shared dungeon is smaller and has none of it.

instance.door.refused.source: That instance is closed to you. Only its owner and their party can enter.

instance.door.unavailable.source: Your instance could not be opened. Try again in a moment.

inventory.batch.aetheric.source: {name} is Aetheric - the Sigil Broker dismantles it, not the Reforge.

inventory.batch.aethericKept.source: {name} is Aetheric, and the Reforge never breaks it.

inventory.batch.artifact.source: {name} is an artifact, and never breaks.

inventory.batch.ask.source: Salvage {n, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}}?

inventory.batch.askShards.source: They are gone for good, and you get {shards}.

inventory.batch.bound.source: {name} is bound to you, and does not break.

inventory.batch.done.source: Salvaged {n, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}}, for {shards}.

inventory.batch.gilded.source: {name} is Gilded - its roll is never broken down.

inventory.batch.kept.source: {kept, plural, one {# would not break and was kept.} other {# would not break and were kept.}}

inventory.batch.worn.source: {name} is worn - take it off to salvage it.

inventory.destroy.gone.source: {n, plural, one {It is gone for good. This cannot be undone.} other {All # are gone for good. This cannot be undone.}}

inventory.destroy.instead.source: {n, plural, one {Destroy it instead? It is gone for good.} other {Destroy all # instead? They are gone for good.}}

inventory.destroy.moved.source: {name} has moved in your pack. Nothing was destroyed.

inventory.sort.how.source: Sort by page, then rarity, name and value. Quest items stay first.

inventory.store.containerFull.source: This container cannot hold any more.

items.refusal.questTwin.source: You already have this quest item.

knight.seatHouse.source: Online, ranks {officer} and {master} are the order's chapter chairs, held by winning Merit. A chair brings no house.

kt.down.source: You are down. A crewmate can raise you within {s} seconds.

legacy.court.cooled.source: {name} stiffens. "That is no way to ask me. Another day."

legacy.rez.refused.source: The realm will not let you rise. Your death stands.

legacy.rez.unheard.source: The realm did not hear the call that would raise you. Another may yet reach you.

legacy.union.born.source: Word reaches you: {child} is born to you and {spouse}.

level.renown.risenStars.source: You have risen to Renown {level}! {stars, plural, one {# new Star shines} other {# new Stars shine}} in your Firmament.

level.renown.subStars.source: Renown {level} · {stars, plural, one {# new Star} other {# new Stars}}

levelup.allMax.source: Every attribute is at its maximum. Leftover points can't be spent.

levelup.blurb.agility.source: Raises your chance to hit and lowers the enemy's chance to hit you.

levelup.blurb.endurance.source: Raises the health you gain each level from now on.

levelup.blurb.enduranceOnline.source: Raises the health you gain each level. Online, your health is never below your class's average for your level at your current Endurance.

levelup.blurb.intelligence.source: Sets your maximum magicka: Intelligence times your class's multiplier.

levelup.blurb.luck.source: Helps you hit and avoid hits, as Agility does, and improves your loot.

levelup.blurb.personality.source: Better prices, friendlier townspeople and better odds in court.

levelup.blurb.speed.source: Makes you move and swing your weapon faster.

levelup.blurb.strength.source: Raises the damage of every hit you land and how much you can carry.

levelup.blurb.willpower.source: Resists spells: a tenth of your Willpower is added to every saving throw.

levelup.howto.source: Click a star to choose it, click again to add a point, right-click to take one back

levelup.role.best.source: Your highest minor skill, the only minor skill that counts toward your next level.

levelup.role.counts.source: Every point counts toward your next level.

levelup.role.dropped.source: Your lowest major skill. It doesn't count toward your next level.

levelup.role.idle.source: Doesn't count toward your next level.

levelup.star.capped.source: a point here won't show for now

levelup.star.title.source: Click to choose, click again to add a point, right-click to take one back

living.adventurer.dareChallenge.source: Think you have what it takes? {gold} gold says you cannot best me in a duel!

living.adventurer.duelChallenge.source: I challenge thee to single combat to test thy blade!

living.adventurer.duelLost.source: Yield! Better luck next time, wanderer. The gold stays with me.

living.adventurer.duelWon.source: A well-fought contest! You have earned my respect and the wager.

living.adventurer.enviousTaunt.source: Another strutting 'hero' thinking they own Tamriel. Step aside before I make you!

living.adventurer.questIntercepted.source: A rival adventurer cleared the dungeon ahead of you and claimed the objective!

living.adventurer.reclaimFailed.source: The rival adventurer refused to yield the prize and walked away.

living.adventurer.reclaimSuccess.source: You have successfully recovered the quest objective from your rival!

living.checkpoint.halt.source: Halt! State your business at this military checkpoint.

living.checkpoint.knightPass.source: Hail, noble Knight! The road is yours; pass freely.

living.checkpoint.passed.source: Papers are in order. Move along, traveller.

living.checkpoint.refused.source: Halt! You shall not pass without authorization!

living.checkpoint.tollDemand.source: Wartime transit requires an inspection toll of {gold} gold.

living.crisis.entry.famine.source: Gaunt townsfolk line the streets of {town}. Famine grips the region.

living.crisis.entry.plague.source: Fever warnings hang at the gates of {town}. Plague stalks the region.

living.crisis.entry.strife.source: Armed patrols march through {town} amid civil strife.

living.crisis.entry.war.source: {town} is under martial law as war rages across the region.

living.economy.famineFood.source: Grain is scarce and provisions fetch a heavy price this season.

living.economy.plaguePotions.source: Remedies and alchemy ingredients are in high demand due to the plague.

living.economy.warShortage.source: Weapons and armor are in short supply due to the ongoing conflict.

living.naval.battleNotice.source: A naval skirmish rages between patrol ships and pirates!

living.nemesis.approach.source: A grim hunter confronts you, holding a contract with your name.

living.nemesis.bribe.source: Gold speaks louder than blood today. Watch your back.

living.nemesis.honor.source: Honor prevails today; our paths may cross again under fairer stars.

living.nemesis.intimidated.source: The challenger shrinks back before your grim gaze and reconsiders their life choices.

living.nemesis.motive.arcane.source: Such powerful artifacts belong in the hands of a master, not an ignorant amateur!

living.nemesis.motive.assassin.source: The Dark Brotherhood sends its regards. You were marked for death.

living.nemesis.motive.bounty.source: There is a fat bounty on your head, criminal. Dead or alive, I collect!

living.nemesis.motive.glory.source: They say you are the fiercest warrior in the land. Let us see if you bleed like one!

living.nemesis.motive.grudge.source: Remember me?! You humiliated me, and now I have returned to pay the blood debt!

living.nemesis.motive.marauder.source: Drop your weapons and empty your purse, traveler! Every coin or your life!

living.nemesis.tauntSuccess.source: The rival sneers and waves their retinue back: 'Stay out of this, fools! This dog is mine alone!'

living.plea.escort.source: The roads crawl with bandits. Might an able blade walk with me to the next crossroads?

living.plea.famine.source: Alms, kind stranger! The granaries are empty and my children weep from hunger. Spare a coin for bread?

living.plea.helped.source: Blessings of the Divines upon you! Tamriel still knows true virtue.

living.plea.parted.source: May Stendarr watch over your journey nonetheless.

living.plea.plague.source: Merciful traveler! My kin is burning with the plague fever. Do you have a healing remedy to spare?

living.plea.rebuffed.source: Curse your cold heart! May misfortune dog your footsteps!

living.plea.war.source: The village was put to the torch by marauders! Please, help us with passage far from this bloodshed!

living.quarantine.gateClosed.source: The city gates are barred due to an outbreak of plague.

living.quarantine.reliefTent.source: A relief healer tent stands outside the locked walls.

living.roadAdv.camp.source: {name} tends a roadside campfire: "Rest your feet by the embers, traveler, if you come in peace."

living.roadAdv.declined.source: "I walk my own path today, wanderer. Perhaps when your purse or renown is heavier."

living.roadAdv.extorted.source: {name} backs down with a scowl and tosses you a pouch of dungeon spoils.

living.roadAdv.intelShared.source: You exchange maps and road warnings over the fire, feeling refreshed for the journey ahead.

living.roadAdv.optionExtort.source: Intimidate (Streetwise): demand a share of their dungeon spoils.

living.roadAdv.optionIntel.source: Trade road news, dungeon intel, and share the camp.

living.roadAdv.optionRecruit.source: Invite to travel and fight alongside you ({gold}g retainer or Etiquette).

living.roadAdv.optionSpar.source: Propose a friendly wager match of blades ({gold}g).

living.roadAdv.parted.source: You exchange a respectful nod and continue along the road.

living.roadAdv.recruited.source: {name} salutes and falls in beside you: "My blade is with you along this road!"

living.roadAdv.skirmish.source: {name} wipes blood from their blade: "Well met! These beasts nearly had the drop on me!"

living.roadAdv.spoils.source: {name} guards a heavy chest of dungeon spoils: "Cleared the crypt ahead. A profitable day for bold steel!"

living.roadAdv.traveling.source: {name} nods along the highway: "Bound for the next delve. Keep your steel sharp on these roads."

living.rumor.famineEnd.source: Relief caravans have reached {region}, easing the famine at last.

living.rumor.famineMid.source: Severe famine starves {region}! Granaries are empty and desperate beggars plead for coin on every road.

living.rumor.famineStart.source: Blighted harvests in {region} have driven up the cost of grain and tavern meals.

living.rumor.plagueEnd.source: The worst of the plague in {region} has passed, and the quarantine cordons are finally lifting.

living.rumor.plagueMid.source: Plague has locked the city gates of {region} under strict quarantine! Only relief tents stand outside.

living.rumor.plagueStart.source: Healers warn of a dark fever spreading through {region}. Best stock up on potions.

living.rumor.strifeEnd.source: The city watch has quelled the worst of the uprising in {region}.

living.rumor.strifeMid.source: Insurgents clash openly with the city watch across {region}!

living.rumor.strifeStart.source: Angry mobs and agitators stir unrest in the streets of {region}.

living.rumor.warEnd.source: A fragile truce holds in {region}, though bands of deserters still roam the highways.

living.rumor.warMid.source: Open war engulfs {region}! Soldiers inspect travelers at road checkpoints and blades cost a fortune.

living.rumor.warStart.source: Scouts report border clashes in {region}. Smiths are already raising prices on steel.

living.travel.ambush.source: You are ambushed along the road!

living.travel.caravan.source: A traveling caravan has made camp along the road.

living.travel.dilemma.source: A stranded traveler waves for assistance.

living.travel.stealthEvadeOption.source: Slip past the ambush undetected through the brush (Stealth).

living.travel.stealthEvaded.source: You slip silently around the highwaymen without a sound.

living.travel.stealthSpotted.source: Your keen stealth spots highwaymen lying in ambush ahead before they notice you!

living.travel.stealthSurpriseOption.source: Strike first from the shadows! (Surprise bonus)

living.urban.orderRestored.source: The guards have restored order in the district.

living.urban.skirmishStart.source: A skirmish erupts in the streets! Townsfolk flee for cover.

livingWorld.friend.court.source: {name} counts you a friend now. You can court them: ask about Courtship under Tell me about.

lock.act.autoWhy.source: Roll your chance to open the lock. A failed roll snaps a pick.

lock.need.source: You need a lockpick to pick this lock.

lock.window.gentle.source: Gentle work is on, so the pins need no timing. Auto attempt rolls your chance. A failed roll snaps a pick.

lock.window.gentlePress.source: Gentle work is on, so the pins are not lifted one by one. Use Auto attempt.

lock.window.keys.source: Left and Right or 1-{n}: choose a pin. Space, Up, W, Enter or a click: lift and set. Q: auto attempt. Esc: leave.

lock.window.start.source: Lift the pins one at a time. The binding pin rises slowly and waits at the line. Press again while it waits to set it.

lock.word.break.source: {count, plural, one {Your lockpick snaps! # left.} other {Your lockpick snaps! # left.}}

lock.word.falseSet.source: A false set. That pin is a spool, cut narrow so it catches early. Lift it and set it again.

lock.word.lift.source: This pin is binding. Press again while it waits at the line.

lock.word.open.source: The plug turns. The lock is open.

lock.word.slip.source: Your pick slips, and a pin drops back.

lock.word.springy.source: That pin springs straight back. It is not binding yet.

lockpick.item.use.source: In Steal mode, activate a locked door, chest or crate to pick it. A pick can snap.

lockpick.item.useLine.source: Switch to Steal mode and activate a locked door, chest or crate to pick its lock.

lockpick.item.what.source: A thin steel pick and a tension wrench, for locks that are not yours.

loot.room.lapsed.source: That take was not confirmed in time, so the item is back where it was.

loot.room.skew.source: Another player here is on a different version of the game, so this can't be opened until you are both on the same one.

lw.cutpurse.0.1.source: My purse! Thief! Stop that thief!

lw.cutpurse.chase.0.0.source: Stop, thief! In the Emperor's name!

lw.cutpurse.chase.0.2.source: Give it back. Now go, and stay off my street.

lw.cutpurse.chase.1.2.source: Back to its owner, that purse.

lw.dice.2.1.source: The gods hate you tonight, friend.

lw.dice.2.2.source: The gods and my creditors both.

lw.flirt.0.1.source: Do I? You've had a cup or two.

lw.flirt.1.1.source: Ask me again when you've washed.

lw.flirt.2.0.source: I saved you the last of the honey cake.

lw.flirt.2.1.source: Did you now. Well. Sit, then.

lw.news.cry.1.source: Letters for {place}! A coin a letter!

lw.news.cry.2.source: Hear ye, people of {town}! The roads are open!

lw.sermon.0.0.source: Hear me, people of {town}! The Eight watch over all who do right!

lw.sermon.0.1.source: Give alms, keep faith, and fear nothing!

lw.sermon.1.0.source: Repent! The gods see every crooked scale in {town}!

lw.sermon.2.1.source: Remember my debts, while you're at it.

lw.watch.beggar.0.0.source: Keep out of the way of the carts, you.

lw.watch.beggar.1.1.source: None, officer. The gods keep you.

lw.watch.beggar.2.2.source: Not a word of it to the others.

lw.watch.buy.0.0.source: One of those, if it's warm.

lw.watch.buy.1.1.source: The same as yesterday, and cheaper.

lw.watch.buy.2.0.source: An apple for a hungry man on duty?

lw.watch.buy.2.1.source: Here. Keep the cutpurses off my stall.

lw.watch.moveAlong.0.0.source: Move along, you. Not in front of the shops.

lw.watch.moveAlong.2.0.source: On your feet. The magistrate comes through today.

lw.watch.word.0.1.source: Quiet enough. The dogs kept me up.

lw.watch.word.1.1.source: Well enough. My roof leaks again.

lw.watch.word.1.2.source: Not a matter for the watch, that.

lw.watch.word.4.1.source: Somebody has to be. You, for one.

lw.watch.word.5.1.source: With you on the street? I'll sleep sound.

madeRules.avoidDeath.source: Stendarr's mercy does not reach here.

madeRules.castOut.source: A death casts you out before the gate.

madeRules.fallDown.source: A death lays you down for {s} seconds: a party member can raise you there. Past it, you fall.

madeRules.finalIn.source: A death is final for this Abyss Dungeon - unless a party member raises you within {s} seconds.

madeRules.noMarkRecall.source: Mark and Recall do not work here.

madeRules.noPenalty.source: A death costs you no gold.

madeRules.potionClock.source: Each kind of potion waits {s} seconds after the last one.

madeRules.regen.source: Regeneration heals at half strength, and not at all for {s} seconds after you are hurt.

madeRules.regenTip.source: Restores health every round - held here: half, and none for {s} seconds after you are hurt.

madeRules.runLeap.source: No running leap: every gap is a plain jump.

madeRules.techFlight.source: A weapon technique cannot carry you over a gap.

madeRules.unstuckHome.source: /unstuck takes you out by the way home.

market.arrived.bought.source: A purchase has arrived: {name} is in your pack.

market.arrived.returned.source: {name} has come back from the market and is in your pack.

market.list.craftedEmpty.source: You carry no crafted piece to sell.

market.list.mwEmpty.source: You carry no Masterwork to auction.

market.list.packEmpty.source: Nothing in your pack can go on the market.

market.list.pickMw.source: Press a Masterwork above to look at it and set its opening bid.

market.list.pickPack.source: Press a piece above to look at it and set its price.

market.list.walledGold.source: Not for a gold sale: {list}. Goods bought with silver sell only for silver, and goods from your pack, or made from them, only go to crafting stations.

market.list.walledGuild.source: Not for the guild Stores: {list}. The guild takes only what you gathered or bought with silver. Goods bought with gold or from your pack stay in your own Stores.

martial.ranger.passiveText.source: Your blows and arrows deal {pct}% more damage to beasts.

martial.ranger.techniqueText.source: Bow: a shot that passes through up to {through} enemies. Long blade: leap at an enemy up to {metres} meters away.

martial.say.standFirm.source: Stand Firm: you hold your ground.

martial.shadowdancer.rider.source: For {seconds} seconds, one enemy blow in {n} misses you.

martial.shadowdancer.techniqueText.source: Dash behind an enemy up to {metres} meters away and strike.

martial.sheet.next.source: {n, plural, one {# martial specialization is open. Choose No, then press W to see the next.} other {# martial specializations are open. Choose No, then press W to see the next.}}

martial.vanguard.rider.source: Each enemy it hits restores {pct}% of your health (up to {foes} enemies).

martial.vanguard.techniqueText.source: Leap up to {metres} meters onto an enemy and hit every enemy within {radius} meters of where you land.

martial.warblade.passiveText.source: Each kill makes you swing {pct}% faster for {seconds} seconds.

martial.warblade.rider.source: For {seconds} seconds, your blows and arrows deal {pct}% more damage.

martial.warblade.techniqueText.source: Hit every enemy in a wide arc in front of you.

martial.windrunner.rider.source: Each enemy it hits restores {pct}% of your fatigue (up to {foes} enemies).

martial.windrunner.techniqueText.source: Bow: {arrows} arrows rain down on a spot. Bare hands: a flying kick at an enemy up to {metres} meters away, even in mid-air.

martial.woodsman.passiveText.source: Each kill restores {pct}% of your fatigue.

martial.woodsman.rider.source: Each enemy it kills restores {pct}% of your health.

martial.woodsman.techniqueText.source: Bow: {arrows} arrows rain down on a spot. Axe: leap onto an enemy up to {metres} meters away.

mods.daggerfallEnemyExpansion.Enabled.de.source: Fifty new enemies - goblins, trolls, minotaurs, golems, mounted knights, necromancers, witches and more - in new encounter tables for every dungeon and climate.

mods.immersiveFootsteps.ArmorSwaySetting.source: Your armor makes a sound as you move
How often armor sounds play. Lower is more often

mods.immersiveFootsteps.Enabled.descript.source: Footsteps that match the ground you walk on, and armour that rattles as you move.

Has no effect here: this game keeps no error log.
Has no effect here: this game keeps no error log.

mods.immersiveFootsteps.FootstepSettings.source: How often footsteps sound. Lower is more often

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.Enabled.de.source: Level up like Oblivion Remastered: every skill you raise fills a 100-point bar, and each level gives you virtues to spend on the attributes you choose. New characters are asked which system they want.

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.allowLuckI.source: Allow Luck to be increased by more than one point

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.attributeP.source: Amount of points for increasing attributes

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.luckIncrea.source: Cost to upgrade Luck by one point

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.majorSkill.source: Points given by a Major Skill level up (100 points required to level up)

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.maxUpdatab.source: The number of attributes to be increased in one level up

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.minorSkill.source: Points given by a Minor Skill level up (100 points required to level up)

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.miscSkills.source: Points given by a Misc Skill level up (100 points required to level up)

mods.oblivionRemasterLeveling.primarySki.source: Points given by a Primary Skill level up (100 points required to level up). Morrowind has no Primary skills, so this starts equal to Major skills.

mods.oceanHoles.Enabled.description.source: Blue holes in the deep sea lead down to flooded dungeons with better loot. About 1 open-sea square in 48 has one: a black hole in the seafloor under a cloud of dark mist. Needs Iliac Puddle No More.

mods.oceanHoles.General.DungeonVisualDar.source: How dark the fog and light are in flooded dungeons

mods.oceanHoles.General.MiasmaHeight.des.source: Height of the mist over a hole

mods.oceanHoles.General.MiasmaParticleCo.source: Amount of mist over a hole

mods.oceanHoles.General.PitSpawnRate.des.source: How many blue holes there are: none at 0, 1 square in 48 at the middle, 1 in 24 at most

mods.pcaao.Enabled.description.source: Armour reduces the damage you take instead of your chance to be hit, your skills decide whether you hit, shields block according to their material, and critical hits multiply damage. Off uses Daggerfall Unity’s combat.

mods.pcaao.armorHitFormulaRedone.descrip.source: Armor reduces the damage you take instead of making you harder to hit.

mods.pcaao.conditionBasedEffectiveness.d.source: Worn weapons and armor work less well. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.pcaao.criticalStrikesIncreaseDamage.source: Critical strikes raise your damage as well as your chance to hit. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.pcaao.equipmentDamageEnhanced.descr.source: Your equipment wears out much faster, depending on its material, what hit it and more.

mods.pcaao.fadingEnchantedItems.descript.source: Enchanted weapons and armor are destroyed when they break in combat. Needs Equipment Damage Enhanced.

mods.pcaao.fixedStrengthDamageModifier.d.source: Strength adds 1 damage per 10 points, as in the classic game, instead of 2.

mods.pcaao.softMaterialRequirements.desc.source: Weapons below the material an enemy needs can still hurt it, at a large damage penalty. Needs Armor Hit Formula Redone.

mods.roadsHazelnut.Enabled.description.source: Hazelnut’s roads, tracks, rivers and streams across the whole Iliac Bay, painted onto the land. Off, the game builds its own roads between the towns on your map.

mods.roadsHazelnut.RiversAndStreams.desc.source: Draws rivers and streams on the land.

mods.roadsHazelnut.SmoothRoads.descripti.source: Lightly smooths road surfaces. Turn it off for slightly better performance.

mods.roleplayRealism.Enabled.description.source: Realism changes: bows by draw weight, no climbing with a weapon out, fairer swing speed and hit chance, bank loans by level, ships only from ports, a heavy-load penalty, lights out when you leave a dungeon, purification that cures poison, reworked class enemies, harsher guild expulsions, and beds you can click to sleep in.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.Gall.source: Enables galloping (sprinting) while riding horses in towns.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.Real.source: Makes the horse and cart movement backwards and sideways more realistic and limited.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.Tram.source: Enables the crime of trampling innocent townsfolk when galloping in a town. Be careful!

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.enha.source: Enable enhanced horse riding module, improving presentation and allowing galloping.

mods.roleplayRealism.EnhancedRiding.foll.source: How much the ride smooths out slopes, from 0 (none) to 32 (most).

mods.roleplayRealism.RefinedTraining.int.source: Enables intensive training option for a session per day for five days, for extra cost.

mods.roleplayRealism.RefinedTraining.var.source: Makes price of training based on skill level as well as player level.

mods.roleplayRealism.advancedArchery.des.source: Alters to-hit and damage done by arrows depending on the length of draw.

mods.roleplayRealism.autoExtinguishLight.source: Automatically extinguish any light sources when you exit a dungeon

mods.roleplayRealism.bandaging.descripti.source: Allows bandages to be used for healing based on medical skill.

mods.roleplayRealism.bedSleeping.descrip.source: Allows sleep to be initiated by clicking on a bed.

mods.roleplayRealism.classicStrengthDama.source: Shows the strength damage bonus at half, as the classic game did.

mods.roleplayRealism.climbingRestriction.source: Prevents climbing with a weapon drawn.

mods.roleplayRealism.encumbranceEffects..source: Provides speed and fatigue penalties when carrying too much weight.

mods.roleplayRealism.enemyAppearance.des.source: Remixes human enemy appearance based on class

mods.roleplayRealism.equipDamage.descrip.source: Increases equipment damage proportional to max condition.

mods.roleplayRealism.loanAmountPerLevel..source: Sets the maximum amount per level that can be borrowed from banks

mods.roleplayRealism.purificationPotion..source: Changes purification potion to cure poison rather than grant invisibility

mods.roleplayRealism.shipPorts.descripti.source: Player can only board their ship when in a port town.

mods.roleplayRealism.underworldExpulsion.source: Enables underworld guilds to expel members for poor performance... with prejudice.

mods.roleplayRealism.variantNpcs.descrip.source: Enable variant NPC sprites in shops & taverns

mods.roleplayRealism.variantResidents.de.source: Fills 80% of houses with the townsfolk you see walking around, instead of random adventurers

mods.roleplayRealism.weaponMaterials.des.source: Moderates the to-hit bonuses of weapon materials so skill remains key factor

mods.roleplayRealism.weaponSpeed.descrip.source: Lowers weapon damage per second for characters with high Speed.

mods.roleplayRealismItems.Enabled.descri.source: Adds 2 new weapons and light and medium armor sets in every metal, and changes what items weigh and cost.

mods.roleplayRealismItems.alchemistPotio.source: Adds random potions for sale at alchemist stores, for a premium price

mods.roleplayRealismItems.bandaging.desc.source: Allows bandages to stack, and to be used for healing based on medical skill

mods.roleplayRealismItems.conditionBased.source: Item prices are based on condition and loot you find can be quite worn out

mods.roleplayRealismItems.lootRebalance..source: Rebalances loot on mobs and in piles

mods.roleplayRealismItems.newArmor.descr.source: Adds new chest, arm, leg and foot armor pieces to the game

mods.roleplayRealismItems.newWeapons.des.source: Adds two new weapons to the game, Archers Axe and Light Flail

mods.roleplayRealismItems.realisticEnemy.source: Enemy equipment is realistic for their class and can be variable condition

mods.roleplayRealismItems.skillBasedStar.source: Player starting equipment is based on skills
Player starting spells are based on skills

mods.roleplayRealismItems.storeQualityIt.source: Items in shops can be in a used condition dependent on the quality of the store

mods.roleplayRealismItems.weaponBalance..source: Balances weapon attack speed and damage ranges against weight to give more valid choices

mods.seasonsIliacBay.Enabled.description.source: Trees, rocks and plants change with autumn, spring and winter. Add your own copy of the mod under Your own textures, or the classic look is used.

mods.shieldWidget.Modules.Inertia.descri.source: Inertia: the shield trails behind as you look around and move.

mods.shieldWidget.Shield.OffsetVertical..source: Offsets the sprite relative to the bottom edge of the screen

mods.shieldWidget.Step.Length.descriptio.source: Size of each step. Higher moves in bigger jumps.

mods.travelOptions.CautiousTravel.SpeedP.source: Speed penalty for travelling cautiously, as a percentage

mods.travelOptions.Enabled.description.source: Choose between the original game’s fast travel and a journey you make yourself, sped up to 60 times, with a panel to steer it. Encounters and places along the way stop you, and you can follow the roads. Off brings back the classic travel map with fast travel only.

mods.travelOptions.FastTravelCostScaling.source: Scales the cost of inns when using standard fast travel, suggest x4-x6 for Climate & Calories.
Scales the cost of ships when using standard fast travel, suggest x2-x3 for Climate & Calories.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowA.source: Allows footstep and hoof sounds during time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowR.source: Has no effect here: Real Grass isn’t included.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowT.source: Allows travel map to target any coordinates using time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AllowW.source: Allows weather effects during time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.AvoidO.source: Steers time accelerated travel around buildings, walls and rocks, and pauses the journey before walking into something it can’t get round.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.FirstP.source: Makes time accelerated journeys in first person, on the ground. Off, the enhanced interface makes them in the Overworld view. Takes effect at once.

With First Person Travel on, journeys follow the roads and tracks as Overworld journeys do, and a place with no way there by land can’t be picked. Off, you head straight for your destination. Takes effect at once.

mods.travelOptions.GeneralOptions.Locati.source: Auto pause when encountering a game location during real time accelerated travel

mods.travelOptions.LocationColours.descr.source: The colour shown on the travel map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Enab.source: Enhances the travel map with larger location dots for cities & towns, and shows roads & tracks with toggle buttons
Adds a streams toggle button separate from rivers button
Enhances the travel map with rivers and streams with a toggle button

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Foll.source: Custom key bind for following paths used if CustomBind set above
Sets the key to initiate time accelerated travelling following paths if roads integration enabled

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Mark.source: The colour used to highlight locations using middle mouse button on travel map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsIntegration.Vari.source: All locations, except for cities & towns, are rendered as smaller dots

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Back.source: The opaque background color to use for the mini-map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Circ.source: Draw the mini-map in a circle around the player

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Filt.source: Pixel filtering to use when rendering the mini-map

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Opaq.source: Render the mini-map with an opaque background color

mods.travelOptions.RoadsJunctionMap.Pers.source: Set this to have the junction mini-map always displayed when following paths

mods.travelOptions.ShipTravel.OnlyToPort.source: Restricts ship travel to be possible only if destination has a port, if from ports setting is enabled

mods.travelOptions.StopAtInnsTravel.Play.source: Enables the stop for night travel option "Inns" to initiate time accelerated travel, instead of fast travel

mods.travelOptions.Teleportation.EnableP.source: Enable paid Mages teleportation service for all guild members, before rank 8

mods.unleveledLoot.Enabled.description.source: Loot and shop stock no longer scale with your level. What materials drop depends on your luck, the shop’s quality and the type of dungeon, and the gold you find follows your luck. Off uses Daggerfall Unity’s rolls.

mods.unleveledLoot.MaterialSwitching.des.source: Whenever this material would drop, change it to the selected material.

mods.warmAshesShips.Enabled.description.source: When you travel by ship, 1 trip in 4 is attacked by pirates. You fight them on deck beside your crew, on a borrowed ship if you don’t own one, then land where you were going.

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.BobWhileIdle.descr.source: Whether the weapon will slightly bob while stationary

mods.weaponWidget.Bob.Offset.description.source: Advances the bob timing. For use with weapon bob.

mods.weaponWidget.Enabled.description.source: Livelier first-person weapons: swings that wind up and recover, the weapon in the hand you swing with, a sheathe animation, a bob as you walk, sway as you look and a kick when you hit or parry. The Morrowind arms move the same way.

Draws a two-handed staff, hammer or flail mirrored in the right hand.
Draws a two-handed sword mirrored in the right hand.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Ambidexterity..source: Ambidexterity: the weapon shows in the hand you swing with (Switch Hand, H), mirrored for the left.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Bob.descriptio.source: Bob: the sprite sways as you walk.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.DoubleScaleTex.source: DoubleScaleTextures: draws the idle pose at double size from the mod’s own textures. Add the mod’s .dfmod under Your own textures.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Inertia.descri.source: Inertia: the weapon trails behind as you look around and move. Needs double-scaled weapon textures.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Offset.descrip.source: Offset: sheathing slides the sprite off the screen and drawing slides it back; a swing returns from below.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Recoil.descrip.source: Recoil: the swing bounces back on a hit, parry or miss, as set below.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Step.descripti.source: Step: the sprite’s position is rounded so it moves in steps.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.Swings.descrip.source: Swings: each strike winds up from the idle pose, plays at its own speed and recovers, in reverse after a hit.

mods.weaponWidget.Modules.TrueTextureSiz.source: TrueTextureSize: a custom texture is drawn at its own pixel size, divided by the scale factor below.

mods.weaponWidget.Offset.Speed.descripti.source: Speed of the slide on and off the screen.

mods.weaponWidget.Recoil.Chance.descript.source: Chance, in percent, of a recoil when the condition is met

ql.line.burningDoors.giver.source: Ysolde Marnhel, Master Conjurer of the Mages Guild of Wayrest

ql.line.burningDoors.lead.source: Someone is opening Dagon’s Breaches on purpose. A Master Conjurer of the Mages Guild wants to know who, and how.

ql.line.covensHoard.giver.source: Ysolde Marnhel, Master Conjurer of the Mages Guild of Wayrest

ql.line.covensHoard.lead.source: Dagon’s covens hoard the Battlespire’s keys in the deep places. Their champions glow gold.

ql.line.honourKey.source: A Weir Key is yours: it waits with your keys.

ql.line.honourKeyHeld.source: The Covens’ Hoard gives one Weir Key to an account, and yours was given already.

ql.line.hourThatWasNot.giver.source: Prior Anselm Vey of the Order of the Hour

ql.line.hourThatWasNot.lead.source: The priests of Akatosh feel a wound in time under the Bay, and brass where there should be stone.

ql.line.introArena.lead.source: The Arena’s Herald is calling for new blood, and pays the first purse in advance of glory.

ql.line.introBay.lead.source: A captain of the watch has more trouble than soldiers: raiders on the roads, and the dead who will not lie down.

ql.line.introCrafts.lead.source: A crafter who works for the court wants an apprentice who can find their own materials.

ql.line.introFirmament.lead.source: An astrologer insists your fortune is written on the Firmament, and that you can write the rest yourself.

ql.line.introGear.lead.source: An armorer offers to show you what a good piece of gear can still be made into.

ql.line.introRoad.lead.source: A stable master knows a merchant yard that pays well for a wagon’s load, if someone will haul it.

ql.line.introSea.lead.source: A harbormaster needs a captain. Any captain. Even you.

ql.line.introTables.lead.source: A tavern regular is looking for someone new to lose to. Or, better, to beat.

ql.line.oldCoil.giver.source: Hamid al-Rasheen, a packet captain of Sentinel

ql.line.oldCoil.lead.source: Sentinel’s sailors say the World-Skin was shed once, and that what was shed still swims.

ql.line.stalled.source: Its next step could not begin here: it will be offered again.

ql.line.thirteenthFrostfall.giver.source: Morwen, a Wyrd Sister of Glenmoril

ql.line.thirteenthFrostfall.lead.source: At the Witches’ Festival the covens sing stars out of the sky. A witch of Glenmoril wants to know why.

ql.line.weirRoad.giver.source: Corvane Tull, Battlemage of the Spire’s last class

ql.line.weirRoad.lead.source: The Battlespire fell in 3E 398. One of its last class of Battlemages has never stopped living that year.

rocket.erupt.source: The mounds erupt and shoot poop into the sky!

rocket.foals.source: Little horses follow it, farting all the way!

rocket.frenzy.source: Daggerfall erupts into a giant diarrhea frenzy!

rocket.great.source: A great horse gallops across the sky, neighing and farting!

rocket.lull.source: The poop subsides. Daggerfall holds its breath.

rocket.rise.source: The ground of Daggerfall rumbles. Mounds push up out of the earth.

rvn.roster.dest.source: {place} - {days, plural, one {a day} other {# days}}, danger {danger}

rvn.roster.gearTip.source: Give it a weapon, armor or a charm from your pack

rvn.roster.heldOff.source: Not worn: it needs an unbroken one-handed weapon

rvn.stars.art.born.source: Its art: {art}. The Grave makes it stronger and quicker.

rvn.stars.art.none.source: It was born without an art. Awakened Art would teach it {art}.

rvn.stars.no.abroad.source: It's away on a mission. Set its stars when it returns.

rvn.stars.no.pointsAfter.source: Reaching this star costs {need} {need, plural, one {point} other {points}}. It has {left}. It gets one point per level after the first, and one per rank past the first.

rvn.stars.no.way.source: This star isn't connected to any star it has taken.

rvn.stars.none.source: No stars taken yet. Start next to the Oath.

rvn.stars.pointsTip.source: One point per level after the first, and one per rank past the first.

rvn.stars.roadLore.source: Missions and loyalty: mission odds, loot, travel time, loyalty and rest.

rvn.stars.stat.awaken.source: Learns an art of its kind, if it was born without one

rvn.stars.stat.bold.source: Brings back nothing if it returns hurt

rvn.stars.stat.hasteShorter.source: Its art can be used again {n} sooner

rvn.stars.tip.backAfter.source: Right-click to remove it and {n, plural, one {the star} other {the # stars}} after it.

rvn.stars.tip.oath.source: Every sworn revenant starts with the Oath. Take a star next to it.

rvn.stars.tip.take.source: Click to take: {n} {n, plural, one {point} other {points}}.

rvn.stars.unaccepted.source: You have unaccepted changes. Press {accept} to keep them, or close again to discard them.

rvn.stars.unacceptedLeave.source: You have unaccepted changes. Press {accept} to keep them, or leave again to discard them.

rvn.sworn.gone.source: It is no longer sworn to you.

rvn.took.home.source: {name} could not keep your {item}. It is back in your pack.

rvn.unq.amb.masteryDo.source: it trains while it waits, and grows bolder every 2 days instead of 3

rvn.unq.amb.plunderDo.source: it raids the roads while it waits, and grows richer the longer you leave it

rvn.unq.amb.vengeanceDo.source: it comes for you sooner, and more often

rvn.unq.ascended.source: {given} will run no more. It is the Dread now, and waits for you in {lair}.

rvn.unq.craft.blinkDo.source: it tears open a rift and is gone. Silence it, hold it, or strike it as it fades

rvn.unq.craft.boltDo.source: it runs faster than anything you have chased. Bring it down from range, and break its will before the killing blow

rvn.unq.craft.sinkDo.source: it sinks into the earth. Strike it before it is under, and it rises, cornered, and runs no more

rvn.unq.craft.smokeDo.source: it throws down smoke and vanishes as it runs, but a blow can still find it

rvn.unq.escape.source: Got away. It will remember this.

rvn.unq.escapeRank.source: Got away and rose to rank {rank}. It will remember this.

rvn.unq.escapeWound.source: It bears the wound you left: {wound}.

rvn.unq.fester.mastery.source: {given} grows bolder. It has been training.

rvn.unq.flee.blink.source: {given} tears open a rift. Strike it before it is through!

rvn.unq.flee.sink.source: {given} sinks into the earth. Strike it before it is under!

rvn.unq.flee.smoke.source: {given} throws down smoke and is lost to sight!

rvn.unq.hunt.dread.source: The Dread will not come to you again. Go to it.

rvn.unq.hunt.trail.source: Weakened, it went to ground here to recover. It will be whole again in {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}.

rvn.unq.omen.mastery.source: Word reaches you that {given} is ready to face you again.

rvn.unq.omen.plunder.source: Travelers speak of {given} on the roads again. It is coming for you.

rvn.unq.omen.vengeance.source: You feel eyes on your back. {given} is hunting you again.

rvn.unq.page.blood.source: If it kills you once more, or fells one more companion, it grows bolder.

rvn.unq.page.craftYoung.source: Its flight: it runs. From rank {rank} it will break away in its own way.

rvn.unq.page.dreadCome.source: It waits for you in {lair} and will not come to you again. Go to it.

rvn.unq.page.dreadStand.source: Last stands: twice in a fight it rises again, at {first}% and at {second}% of its health.

rvn.unq.page.dreadWill.source: At home it has nowhere to run: it never flees, and kneels at the end.

rvn.unq.page.heals.source: The oldest heals in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} unless you find it first.

rvn.unq.page.how.source: An elite or champion marked Unquiet that escapes you, or kills you, will remember you and come back for you.

rvn.unq.page.howHeld.source: From Renown {renown}, an elite or champion marked Unquiet that escapes you, or kills you, will remember you and come back for you.

rvn.unq.page.noneYet.source: No foe has earned your name yet.

rvn.unq.page.tears.source: If its will holds at your killing blow once more, it grows bolder.

rvn.unq.page.woundedCome.source: Recovering in {lair}, whole again in {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}. Find it there.

rvn.unq.rumor.dread.source: They say {name} has gone to ground in {lair}, and that nobody who goes in comes out.

rvn.unq.rumor.mastery.source: Word is it trains day and night for the day it meets you again.

rvn.unq.rumor.plunder.source: Word is it has been raiding the roads.

rvn.unq.rumor.vengeance.source: Word is it asks after you by name.

rvn.unq.slip.source: You hesitated. {given} got away, and it will remember.

rvn.unq.trail.source: Its trail leads to {lair}, where it has gone to ground to recover. Catch it before it is whole again.

rvn.unq.trained.source: {given} has been training. It has learned to answer your {how}.

rvn.unq.wound.bledDo.source: a wound that will not close, so it has less health

rvn.unq.wound.crackedDo.source: cracked bones, so it staggers more easily

rvn.unq.wound.lamedDo.source: a lamed leg, so it runs slower

rvn.unq.wound.maimedDo.source: a maimed hand, so its blows are lighter

saddle.note.failing.source: The {wagon} is failing. Mend it to restore its pace

saddle.note.load.source: Overloaded. Your team pulls it more slowly

saddle.note.rickety.source: The {wagon} is rickety. A repair kit or a Wagon Yard will mend it

saddle.note.starvingGallop.source: Starving. It will not gallop until it eats

saddle.note.winded.source: Winded. Ease off and let it breathe

schools.open.whereGrowth.source: See them all and choose one on the Growth tab of the pause menu.

schools.say.foresight.source: Foresight: you saw the blow coming.

schools.spellbreaker.passiveText.source: Enemies' saving throws against your damage spells are {points} lower.

schools.spellbreaker.rider.source: On a hit, refunds {pct}% of its magicka cost.

schools.trickster.passiveText.source: When damage drops you below {pct}% health, you turn invisible for {rounds} rounds. This can happen once every {minutes} minutes.

schools.trickster.rider.source: If it takes hold, you gain Chameleon for {rounds} rounds.

schools.warden.passiveText.source: While your Shield holds, you regain {pct}% of your health each round.

schools.warden.rider.source: For {seconds} seconds, enemy blows deal {pct}% less damage to you.

schools.wardwright.rider.source: For {seconds} seconds, each Destruction spell that hits you has a {pct}% chance to be absorbed, if you have room for the magicka.

season.tremor.1.source: The ground heaves. Steam hisses out of cracks in the earth.

season.tremor.2.source: The earth roars. Deep below, something vast is waking.

seat.bounty.denPaid.source: The Bounty pays you {n} silver for the den.

seat.edict.bountyDens.source: Outlaws' hideouts and lairs near the town: the treasury pays {silver} silver a den cleared, from what is set aside.

seat.gift.choice.source: {material}: {stores, number} in your Stores, {bag, number} in your bag

seat.gift.counted.source: It counts as influence for your guild here.

seat.gift.doneStockpile.source: You gave {n, number} {material} to the stockpile at {seat}.

seat.gift.none.source: You hold none of what it takes, in your Stores or your bag.

seat.gift.ruleCamp.source: Any member may give materials from their Stores or their bag - what they gathered, made or bought with silver, never with gold. The Siege Camp is spent at the Turning on the siege it is raised for, and nothing given comes back. Each unit you gathered or made counts 1 influence a silver of its value for your guild here, as a seat writ's delivery does.

seat.gift.ruleStockpile.source: Any member may give materials from their Stores or their bag - what they gathered, made or bought with silver, never with gold. The works take what they need from the stockpile, and nothing given comes back. Each unit you gathered or made counts 1 influence a silver of its value for your guild here, as a seat writ's delivery does.

seat.gift.uncounted.source: It counts no influence this week: only a member seven days in the guild, whose account fights for it this week, counts.

seat.holding.tab.source: {town} is a holding of {charter}. Its Charter is won, held and besieged at {seat}, and everything given or earned here counts there.

shop.aurum.lineAll.source: Aurum buys every item in the shop and in the Folios. Your deeds find it, the week's deeds pay it, and you can buy it here.

shop.aurum.rules.source: Aurum has no cash value. It cannot be traded, and it buys no power.

shop.bundle.held.source: Owned: its price is taken off

shop.bundle.part.source: Partly owned: its price is less

shop.cosmetic.source: Every item is cosmetic. It gives no power in the game.

shop.deals.line.source: Each costs a quarter less today. New deals come each day at midnight UTC.

shop.deed.line.source: Each deed pays once a week. A new week starts on Monday, UTC.

shop.look.aurbis.source: The wheel of the heavens about Aetherius, its spheres turning in their orbits. It moves.

shop.look.aurumAll.source: Aurum for every item in the shop and in the Folios. It has no cash value and cannot be traded.

shop.look.azurastar.source: Azura's Star turning slowly in the dusk, its heart of light pulsing. It moves.

shop.look.daedricchampion.source: Daedric Dominion, the Daedric Pyre, Eternal Champion and the Oblivion Sigil, together.

shop.look.dawnbringer.source: A title on a plate of gold, rays of dawn rising behind its letters, over your name.

shop.look.dominion.source: A ring of Daedric script burns black and crimson at your feet, embers rising off it. It comes in three bundles.

shop.look.elderscroll.source: An Elder Scroll open between gilded rollers, its script lit line by line. It moves.

shop.look.eternal.source: A cape of blue-violet fire on your back. It flows as you move, and wisps of flame trail behind you.

shop.look.eternalchampion.source: A title on a plate of crimson fire under a gold edge, over your name.

shop.look.gatefire.source: Dagon's Breach between black spires, its fire turning, embers rising. It moves.

shop.look.gatesigil.source: A gate of runes, a spark burning between its pillars. It comes in the Portal Master bundle.

shop.look.genesis.source: A title set on a plate of blue-violet fire that burns behind its letters, over your name.

shop.look.hourglass.source: A gilded hourglass that turns over when its last grain falls. It moves.

shop.look.lordofoblivion.source: The Daedric Warhorse, the Daedric Stone, Daedric Dominion and the Daedric Pyre, together.

shop.look.oblivion.source: A Daedric sigil, its spokes burning crimson round a dark eye. It comes in the Daedric Champion bundle.

shop.look.origin.source: A dragon coiled round on itself, biting its tail, a spark burning at its heart. Light runs round its scales.

shop.look.portalmaster.source: The Daedric Stone, Daedric Dominion and the Gate Sigil, together.

shop.look.redmountain.source: Red Mountain under its ash, lava running down its flanks, smoke rising. It moves.

shop.look.sanguinerose.source: A black-red rose in full bloom, dew on its petals, thorns along its stem.

shop.look.voidwalker.source: A title on a plate of violet void, stars drawn slowly into its dark, over your name.

shop.look.whitegold.source: The White-Gold Tower over the Imperial City and Lake Rumare at dusk.

shop.noPreview.source: This device cannot show the aura here.

shop.noPreviewArmory.source: This device cannot show the piece here.

shop.noPreviewEffect.source: This device cannot show the effect here.

shop.pass.closedFolios.source: The Folios are not open yet.

shop.pass.found.source: Aurum found today: {n, number} of {max, number}

shop.pass.foundLine.source: Deeds find Aurum each day, up to a limit. Challenges pay their Aurum beside it.

shop.pass.freeLine.source: Every registered account can buy from it.

shop.pass.howFolios.source: Spend Aurum on any item of an open page. Each page opens once you spend enough in its folio. The folios never close.

shop.pass.overFolios.source: The season is over, and its challenges with it. Its folios stay open.

shop.pass.pageFolioLocked.source: Unlock this folio to open this page.

shop.pass.premiumLine.source: Unlock it once with Aurum, then buy its items. It never expires.

shop.pass.premiumOpen.source: Unlocked. It is yours for good.

shop.pass.signInFolios.source: Sign in with a username to buy from the Folios.

shop.proceeds.source: All proceeds go to the costs of developing DFO Online.

shop.stripe.source: Payments are taken by Stripe. Prices are in US dollars, and Stripe can show your own currency and ways to pay. No card details reach the game.

shop.who.closed.source: The shop does not take payments yet.

shop.who.for.source: Purchases go to the account {name}, for every character on it.

shop.who.guest.source: A guest account cannot buy. Add a username from your profile first.

shop.who.out.source: Sign in from your profile to buy.

shop.who.unread.source: The shop could not be read. Open it again when you are online.

skin.layered.own.source: Your character's own body, until you choose one.

social.guild.castle.none.source: A guild that holds a crown's Charter - Daggerfall, Wayrest, Sentinel or a province's capital, but the Imperial City - may buy its castle for {price, number} silver from the treasury: its own instance of the castle, which only its members can enter. The castle goes with the Charter: if the region is lost, half its price comes home.

social.guild.castle.short.source: the treasury holds too little silver

social.guild.castle.sold.source: The castle is given up. {back} silver came home.

start.BlackMarsh.body.source: Smugglers seized the Emperor's courier on the road from Helstrom and carried his satchel into a ruin in the marsh. Your sealed orders are in it.

start.Elsweyr.body.source: Bandits took a caravan of Dwemer brass bound for Sentinel, and the Emperor's courier who rode with it. Your sealed orders are somewhere in their hold.

start.IliacBay.body.source: Your ship to Daggerfall goes down in a storm, and you wake in a pirates' cave on the coast. The Emperor's sealed orders were lost in the wreck. The tide may have carried them in.

start.Imperial.body.source: The Blades test the Emperor's agents before they trust them. Your sealed orders lie at the heart of a disused prison near the Imperial City. Bring them out, and you have passed.

start.Imperial.where.source: An old prison near the Imperial City

start.Morrowind.body.source: Diggers near Mournhold broke through into old Dwemer halls and fled what they found. The Emperor's courier went down after them with your sealed orders. Neither came back up.

start.Skyrim.body.source: The Emperor's courier sheltered from a blizzard in an old hall near Solitude, where the dead do not rest. He carried your sealed orders, and he never came out. You go in after him.

start.Sumurset.body.source: A scholar of the Mantella was to hand you the Emperor's sealed orders. She was found dead in the hall near Alinor where she kept her notes, and the orders are still inside.

start.Valenwood.body.source: A wounded Blades courier crawled into a cave near Falinesti to hide from the men hunting her. She carried your sealed orders. Find her.

start.Valenwood.where.source: A cave under the roots near Falinesti

start.noSite.source: No way to that province could be found. Your story begins in the Iliac Bay.

start.page.hint.source: Click one, or up/down and Enter, or press 1 to {n}

start.page.lead.source: Choose where this character wakes. Wherever it is, the Emperor's orders send you to Daggerfall, and the main story begins when you get there.

start.page.shut.source: The land past the Bay is off

survival.boon.mealTip.source: A hearty tavern meal: you stay fed and your thirst is held while it lasts.

tutorials.chapters.body1.source: Online, quests raise your standing with each guild by at most {max} a real day (days start at midnight UTC). Any more is added on later days.

tutorials.chapters.body2.source: Reviews promote you up to rank {cap}. Ranks {officer} and {master} are chapter chairs, won by Merit at each Sunday's Turning. A notice board explains chapters.

tutorials.chapters.trigger.source: When you first come online as a member of a guild, temple or order.

tutorials.characterSheet.skillRaise.source: A used skill goes up when you rest or travel, at most once every 6 hours.

tutorials.characterSheet.skillRaiseStats.source: A used skill goes up when you rest or travel, at most once every 6 hours. Your Stats page shows how close each skill is.

tutorials.crafting.body.source: Online, stand at a station and press {Professions}: the Crafting page opens on it. Cook at any fire.

tutorials.crafting.more.source: Your home can hold stations too. Each crafting profession under {Professions} says more.

tutorials.crafting.shops1.source: Forge: Weaponsmiths, Armorers. Loom: Clothing Stores. Workbench: Furniture Stores, joineries.

tutorials.crafting.shops2.source: Jeweler's bench: Pawn Shops, Gem Stores. Mason's bench: General Stores. Alchemy: Alchemists, Mages Guilds. Enchanting: Mages Guild halls.

tutorials.guilds.body1.source: Join a guild for its services and its work. Do that work and practice the skills it teaches to rise in rank.

tutorials.guilds.body2.source: You may join one temple, one knightly order, and as many guilds as will have you.

tutorials.guilds.online.source: Online, reviews promote you no further than rank {cap}. Ranks {officer} and {master} are chapter chairs; see Guild Chapters.

tutorials.guilds.trigger.source: When you first visit a guild.

tutorials.kingsGambit.body1.source: A game of armies and kings, played on a board laid across a tavern's card table. Choose a regular to play, set down your stake and raise your army.

tutorials.kingsGambit.body2.source: Each turn, move your pieces, strike and drink potions. Bring down the enemy king to win, and guard your own.

tutorials.kingsGambit.trigger.source: When you first sit down to The King's Gambit.

tutorials.questlines.body1.source: The Quests tab lists what each quest asks of you and ticks off each step. Some quests make you choose, and end differently for each choice.

tutorials.questlines.gearBody.source: Some quests, once finished, let you pick one of three pieces of gear: the quest’s page says so. Questlines are longer stories told in several quests, one after another. The same tab lists them.

tutorials.questlines.trigger.source: When you first take a quest with objectives.
